reviewQueue.why: CHALLENGER DOWNGRADE. The level treatment is a coin-flip presented as settled. Rule 1 lists "כשר" as a level word (=regular) and Rule 5 says record BOTH when a string states an authority and a level; Rule 3 lists a leading "כשר" as a strippable qualifier. The proposer invoked Rule 3 to drop the level here but Rule 5 to extract "מהדרין" from the parallel strings in the same batch (כשר למהדרין בד"ץ בית יוסף, כשר בד"ץ בית יוסף מהדרין), and never reconciled the two readings. Downstream this splits identically-tiered records: the ~276 bare "כשר" rows get level=regular while these ~16 get level=null, so they fall out of BOTH a regular filter and a mehadrin filter. The authority is correct and must be kept. Do NOT resolve this by setting level="regular" — that would misrepresent a Sephardi bassar-chalak badatz. Needs a project-wide policy call on bare "כשר".

CHALLENGER VERDICT: WRONG. Invents an authority out of a level word. The proposed id "badatz-mehadrin-jerusalem" was assembled from bare "בד"ץ" + the level word "מהדרין" + a city; Rule 1 states both name NO authority, and Rule 4 licenses a city only when paired with רבנות / הרבנות / מועצה דתית. No certifier trades under this name; what exists is the Jerusalem Religious Council's own כשרות מהדרין tier, and the dataset carries רבנות ירושלים מהדרין 39x, רבנות מהדרין ירושלים 2x, מועצה דתית ירושלים מהדרין 1x. Minting the id would plant a phantom independent haredi badatz that a user who does not accept Rabbanut-mehadrin would read as a stricter hechsher than it is. The refusal to merge into rabbinate-jerusalem is correct (Rule 2) and is preserved: authorityId null, mehadrin level retained.

notes:
261 raw values consolidated: 203 auto-applied aliases (proposer "certain" AND challenger "sound") and 58 sent to review. 81 authorities, every one of them referenced by at least one alias, and no alias points at an unregistered id. All three "wrong" verdicts (בד"ץ מהדרין ירושלים, בד"ץ קהילות קריית ספר, בד"ץ ביתר / מהדרין) and all ten "downgrade-to-uncertain" verdicts are in the review queue; none reached aliases. Every raw is copied byte-for-byte and the whole set was checked programmatically (scratchpad registry.json + validate.mjs) for duplicate raws (none), overlap between aliases and reviewQueue (none), duplicate authority ids or Hebrew names (none), unregistered alias authorities (none), unused authorities (none), and aliases whose raw contains מהדרין while level is null (none).

DEDUPES — the same real body was proposed under two ids; two registry entries for one body is a defect, so they were merged:
1. rabbinate-ness-ziona + rabbinate-nes-ziona -> rabbinate-nes-ziona (רבנות נס ציונה and רבנות מהדרין נס ציונה are one city rabbinate).
2. rabbinate-lower-galilee + rabbinate-galil-tachton -> rabbinate-galil-tachton (רבנות גליל תחתון / רבנות הגליל התחתון differ only by the ה prefix, Rule 3).
3. rabbinate-modiin + rabbinate-modiin-maccabim-reut -> rabbinate-modiin-maccabim-reut. מודיעין is the short name of the city מודיעין-מכבים-רעות; the explicit id was chosen because the dataset also contains מודיעין עילית and חבל מודיעין, which stay separate bodies (rabbinate-modiin-illit, rabbinate-hevel-modiin). Only the three strings the challenger vouched for as city-of-Modiin were merged; the bare "רבנות מודיעין" is in the review queue.
4. rav-rubin, rav-machpud and rav-landau each arrived under several authorityNames (כשרות ..., בד"ץ ..., בד"צ מהדרין - ...). One entry each; the canonical Hebrew name was chosen and the level word was kept out of it.

LEVEL-ONLY ALIASES (11, authorityId null with the level preserved — the intended honest result): מהדרין, כשר למהדרין, כשר מהדרין, בד"ץ מהדרין, כשר למהדרין בד"ץ, רבנות מהדרין, רבנות מקומית מהדרין, רבונות מקומית מהדרין, הרבנות המקומית כשרות מהדרין, כשר (regular), כשר רבנות (regular).
NO-INFORMATION ALIASES (12, both fields null): רבנות, הרבנות, רבנות מקומית, הרבנות המקומית, הרבנות האזורית, הרבנות האיזורית, רבנות המועצה האזורית, בד"ץ, כשר בד"ץ, כשרות רבנות ובד"ץ, כשרות מקומית, רב הקיבוץ. They are auto-applied so these strings are recorded as resolved-to-nothing rather than being re-queued on every pass.

OPEN DECISIONS a human must make — each one interacts with already-applied aliases:
- Bare "כשר" policy. Two queued items (כשר בד"ץ בית יוסף, כשר בהשגחת רבנות אריאל) turn on whether a leading כשר states the regular level or is a strippable qualifier. The bare string "כשר" itself IS applied as level=regular, so the output is internally inconsistent until the policy is set. Do not resolve כשר בד"ץ בית יוסף to regular — Beit Yosef is a Sephardi bassar-chalak badatz.
